## Requirement delivery: Enforced authored commits and measured quality

### Acceptance Criteria

1. At least 1.0 nonblank noncomment meaningful test LOC per newly added or materially changed executable production LOC, including adopted upstream source, measured per task and merged feature; fixtures, snapshots, repeated trivial assertions and generated boilerplate cannot inflate numerator. Exact baseline and file classifications recorded.
2. 100 percent newly introduced or changed executable statements, branches and functions covered by passing behavior tests, including adopted source. Carry upstream tests and provenance where available; adoption grants no coverage exemption. Missing meaningful tests must be written. Report imported lines separately without excluding them from required totals. No task marked done with a failing required metric.
3. Before first implementation commit install scoped commit helper, prepare-commit-msg/commit-msg validation and pre-integration/pre-push all-commit audit. Validate identity sequence, exact format, date, branch at creation, staged tree and footer; existing history exempt by recorded baselines. No --no-verify, skipped hooks, forced acceptance or rewriting prior history. No commits during spec preparation before this prerequisite.

## Requirement product: Complete approved production UI redesign

### Acceptance Criteria

1. All214 existing mapped screens and all17 miniapps remain reachable and useful under approved layout and real hosted/OSS constraints. No capability silently dropped; customer workflows use real APIs.

## Requirement windows: Hosted Windows Electron application

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Windows x64 NSIS executable, Gideon product identity/icon, checksum manifest, installation/start/uninstall evidence. Build cross-platform through Node script; use Windows runner for native qualification. No update server or signing claim without configured service/credentials.
2. Hosted web experience inside Windows Electron, adapting existing desktop package. Windows hosted mode never requires or starts a POSIX local backend. Existing Mac/Linux local runtime behavior retained.
